model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: NOT revenue. FY2025 Adjusted Recurring Earnings (EPRA recurring earnings after external NCI and after the hybrid coupon), Group share, EUR Mn. H1-2026 report, EPRA table line 2115. This is the post-interest, post-tax, post-hybrid stream the engine compounds; the AFFO deduction is modelled as capex_pct_path.
inputs.share_count_basis: EPRA fully diluted 148,820,733 at 2026-06-30 (H1-2026 report line 1811), the same basis as the EPRA NTA/NRV per share. Shares outstanding (undiluted) were 144,472,611 and the H1-2026 average undiluted 143,961,862 on which AREPS is struck; using the diluted count is ~3% conservative versus guided AREPS. Held FLAT: IFRS 2 share-based payment (EUR 24.5 Mn FY2025) is already expensed inside Adjusted Recurring Earnings, so growing the count would double-count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Set to ZERO deliberately. Adjusted Recurring Earnings is already after recurring financial expenses and the hybrid coupon, so the flow is capitalised at the cost of equity and no debt is deducted again (SKILL.md: never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow). Actual balance sheet 2026-06-30: IFRS net debt excl. hybrid EUR 18.6 Bn, incl. hybrid EUR 20.1 Bn (hybrids EUR 1.5 Bn: 815 Mn 4.875% NC2030 + 685 Mn 4.750% NC2031); gross borrowings per CSV EUR 22,974 Mn, cash EUR 2,836 Mn; LTV incl. hybrid 41.9%; net debt/EBITDA incl. hybrid 9.1x; average cost of debt 2.3% (2.1% FY2025).
inputs.last_fcf_definition: Owner AFFO FY2025 = Adjusted Recurring Earnings 1,371.5 - maintenance capex 115.6 - leasing capex 96.7 - tenant incentives/letting fees ~12 (FY2025 URD lines 19359-19363 and the 'Other' capex line). Development, extension and like-for-like refurbishment capex (EUR 402 Mn + 373 Mn Group share in 2025) is growth capex funded by disposals under the EUR 600 Mn/yr net capex cap and is NOT charged; its return shows up in the growth path.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Cash-flow statement OCF 2,046.5 less capex 894.9 (CSV FY2025). Coincidentally close to owner AFFO; it is NOT the basis of the model because it is pre-interest-on-hybrids and post-development-capex.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD statement of changes in equity, share-based payment 24.6 (line 21287); CSV StockBasedComp 24.5. Already expensed inside Adjusted Recurring Earnings -- not deducted a second time.
inputs.interest_income_note: The KPI 'InterestIncome' series (EUR 384 Mn FY2025) is interest income on economic hedging instruments, netted inside recurring financial expenses; it is not surplus-cash yield and is not deducted.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:22Z regular close (Euronext Paris); re-checked 2026-10-26 before the Paris open, unchanged
inputs.guidance_fy2026: AREPS EUR 9.15-9.30 (confirmed at H1-2026, line 612); EUR 5.50/share distribution for FY2026 (line 617); payout 60-70% of AREPS from FY2027; EUR 3.1 Bn minimum total distributions FY2025-28; LTV incl. hybrid to ~40% and net debt/EBITDA incl. hybrid to ~8.0x by 2028; net capex capped at EUR 600 Mn/yr from 2026 (2026 envelope ~EUR 0.7 Bn after 2025 deferrals).
inputs.wacc_rationale: This is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, built in EUR: risk-free 3.0% (blend of 10y Bund ~2.7% and 10y OAT ~3.4%, Oct-2026), ERP 5.5%, equity beta 1.2 for a 9.1x net debt/EBITDA, 42% LTV mall REIT = 9.6%, rounded to 9.5% base; 8.5% bull (rates ease, deleveraging to 8x delivered) and 10.5% bear (rate upswing, cap-rate expansion). The flow being capitalised is after all interest and hybrid coupons, so financing cost is charged once, inside the flow.
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS 16 lease interest (EUR 61.7 Mn FY2025) and financial-lease costs sit inside recurring financial expenses and are therefore already inside Adjusted Recurring Earnings; no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path = 0).
inputs.nci_treatment: External non-controlling interests (EUR 29.6 Mn FY2025) are deducted inside the EPRA recurring earnings line before the hybrid coupon; the flow is Group share. No separate NCI bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing: REIT / property trust, IAS 40 fair-value). Rationale: URW's IFRS net income is dominated by revaluation (FY2020 -7.2 Bn, FY2023 -1.6 Bn, FY2025 +1.3 Bn) so P/E and net margin are meaningless, and an owner-FCF DCF at WACC with net debt subtracted would charge the EUR 20 Bn of debt twice against a post-interest stream. Mapping onto the engine: base_revenue = Adjusted Recurring Earnings (post-interest, post-tax, post-NCI, post-hybrid), ebitda_margin 100%, SBC/D&A/tax 0 (all inside the flow), capex_pct_path = maintenance + leasing capex as % of the flow (AREPS -> AFFO), wacc field = cost of equity, net_debt = 0, terminal cap non-binding. The growth path is a path for Adjusted Recurring Earnings in total EUR, not per share. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Cross-check: EPRA NTA EUR 115.60 and NRV EUR 146.80 at 2026-06-30 are recorded in inputs.epra_nav_2026_06_30; the base AFFO value should sit at a discount to NTA consistent with a 9.5% cost of equity on a 7.5-8% AFFO yield on NTA, and the bull case should not exceed NRV. Price is the last regular close; no earnings print pending within the week (FY2026 results due Feb-2027).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: like-for-like NRI growth (+4.5% H1-2026) net of rising average cost of debt (2.1% -> 2.3% and climbing as low-coupon debt rolls), disposals and lower indexation; anchored between the 3-yr AREPS CAGR (+1.0%, FY2022-25) and the 10-year AREPS trend
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: IFRS EPS CAGRs are not computed: net result is dominated by fair-value revaluations (FY2020 -52.10, FY2025 +8.86) and carries no information about the recurring stream. Shareholders' equity CAGR is negative (-2.6% 3-yr) because of 2020-23 devaluations and the resumption of distributions, not because the recurring business shrank. Reported FCF 5-yr CAGR (+34.8%) starts from the COVID trough FY2020 and is not a trend. The AREPS series is the operative one: 9.31 -> 9.62 -> 9.85 -> 9.58 FY2022-25, i.e. +1.0% CAGR with FY2025 down -2.7% on disposals, the Olympics comp and the hybrid re-coupon.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue (IFRS, incl. property services and C&E) FY2022 2,683 -> FY2025 2,676; FY2020 2,329 -> FY2025 2,676. Owner AFFO history is not reconstructable before FY2023 from the CSV because maintenance/leasing capex is only split in the MD&A; the fcf CAGRs above are on reported cash-flow FCF (1,531 FY2022 -> 1,152 FY2025; 259 FY2020 -> 1,152 FY2025).

base.growth_rates_rationale: Y1 (FY2026): guidance midpoint AREPS 9.225 x ~144.3 Mn average undiluted shares = EUR 1,331 Mn, -2.9% on FY2025's 1,371.5 (disposals, lower indexation, stronger EUR, higher cost of debt). Y2-Y4: +3.0% = like-for-like NRI growth of ~4% plus 2025-26 deliveries (Hamburg-Ueberseequartier, Porte de Versailles) and Westfield Rise, less ~1pt/yr of financing drag as the 2.3% average cost of debt rolls toward 3%+. Y5-Y7 2.5%, Y8-Y10 2.0% fading to indexation. No AREPS target for 2028 is published; the EUR 3.1 Bn distribution floor and 60-70% payout from FY2027 are consistent with AREPS of ~EUR 9.3-9.8 by 2028, which this path reaches.
base.capex_rationale: 16.5% of the flow = EUR 212 Mn maintenance + leasing capex plus ~EUR 12 Mn tenant incentives/letting fees in FY2025 (16.3% of 1,371.5), grown with the flow. Excludes development, extension and like-for-like refurbishment capex, which is funded by disposals under the EUR 600 Mn/yr cap and returns through the growth path.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.0% = European CPI indexation less a small structural drag from retail format risk. Implied terminal AFFO multiple 13.6x at 9.5%/2.0%, i.e. a 7.4% AFFO yield, inside the 6.5-8% range at which prime European mall portfolios have traded 2023-26. Cap of 20x is non-binding.

bull.growth_rates_rationale: Y1 at the top of guidance (AREPS 9.30 -> EUR 1,342 Mn, -2.1%); then +4.5% as like-for-like NRI growth holds at 4-5%, Westfield Rise and Saudi franchising scale, and the deleveraging to 8x by 2028 lets the hybrids be refinanced cheaper; cost of equity 8.5% on lower rates; terminal multiple 17.1x (5.9% AFFO yield). Bull value should sit at or below EPRA NRV EUR 146.80.

bear.growth_rates_rationale: Y1 a small miss of the guidance floor (AREPS ~9.08, -4.5%) on a consumer slowdown and FX; Y2-Y3 flat as refinancing at 3.5-4% absorbs all NRI growth and further disposals shrink the base; 1-1.5% thereafter. Capex at 21% charges part of the like-for-like refurbishment spend as non-discretionary (format defence against e-commerce). Cost of equity 10.5% on a rate upswing; terminal 1.0%; terminal multiple 10.6x (9.4% AFFO yield).

scenario_narratives.base: URW delivers FY2026 AREPS at the guidance midpoint (EUR 9.225), then compounds Adjusted Recurring Earnings at ~3% for three years and 2-2.5% thereafter: like-for-like NRI growth of ~4% (record-low 4.1% vacancy, OCR 14.6%, MGR uplift +10.6%) net of a rising average cost of debt as 2.1-2.3% legacy debt rolls to 3%+. Maintenance and leasing capex absorb ~16.5% of the flow, leaving AFFO of ~EUR 7.5/diluted share in FY2026 against a EUR 5.50 distribution. Capitalised at a 9.5% EUR cost of equity with 2.0% terminal growth, the value sits at a discount to EPRA NTA (EUR 115.60) consistent with the market applying an equity-risk premium to a 42% LTV portfolio rather than paying appraised value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Guidance top end in FY2026, then 4-4.5% growth as Westfield Rise, Saudi franchising fees and the 2025-26 deliveries add to 4-5% like-for-like NRI, while the deleveraging to ~8x by 2028 and easier EUR rates bring the cost of equity to 8.5% and allow the EUR 1.5 Bn of hybrids to be refinanced cheaper. The NAV discount narrows toward NTA; value is bounded above by EPRA NRV (EUR 146.80).
scenario_narratives.bear: A consumer slowdown and FX headwind push FY2026 AREPS slightly below the EUR 9.15 floor; from 2027 refinancing at 3.5-4% and continued non-core disposals absorb all NRI growth for two years, and a rate upswing re-expands cap rates, reversing the 2025-26 revaluation gains and stalling the LTV path. Format-defence capex becomes non-discretionary (21% of the flow). Cost of equity 10.5%, terminal growth 1.0%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default: the balance sheet (9.1x net debt/EBITDA incl. hybrid, 42% LTV, BBB+/Baa2) makes the equity a levered claim on cap rates, so the downside tail (rate upswing, revaluation reversal, refinancing drag) deserves equal weight to the upside tail (NAV discount closing). Nothing in the record (guidance met FY2023-25, first positive revaluation since 2018 in 2025, vacancy at record low) argues for a bear weight above 25%.

entry_price.hurdle_rationale: 12% rather than the 15% growth-equity hurdle: the flow is a post-interest, indexation-linked rental stream with a 6.1% cash distribution yield at the current price; 15% would demand an entry AFFO yield above 13%, a level at which the 2021-22 rights-issue trough traded only briefly.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Capitalise what the owner actually receives -- Adjusted Recurring Earnings after all financing cost and hybrid coupons, less the maintenance and leasing capex needed to keep the centres leased -- at a EUR cost of equity that reflects 9x leverage, and never deduct the debt a second time. Growth is NRI indexation plus deliveries net of the financing drag; development capex is treated as self-funded by disposals under the EUR 600 Mn cap. EPRA NTA (EUR 115.60) and NRV (EUR 146.80) are the cross-check: base should sit below NTA, bull below NRV.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest rates: every 100 bp on the cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 15%; the 2.3% average cost of debt rolls toward market rates over 7 years and the growth path assumes ~1 pt/yr of drag -- a faster roll or wider spreads would push the base toward the bear path
Leverage: 9.1x net debt/EBITDA and 42% LTV incl. hybrid leave little covenant headroom if valuations reverse; the 2028 targets (8x, 40%) depend on disposals at or near book
AFFO definition: charging the full like-for-like refurbishment capex (EUR 373 Mn FY2025) would cut AFFO by ~27% and the base value by about the same; the model treats it as growth capex
US strategy reversal (exit announced 2023, retain-and-grow since Feb 2025) and continued trophy-asset purchases (Southcenter, UTC) add execution risk to the capex cap
Share-count basis: valued on 148.8 Mn EPRA fully diluted shares; on the 144.5 Mn outstanding the per-share values are ~3% higher
